title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used to conduct a cyberattack following initial compromise of a system through a known vulnerability in marimo notebook software. After an attacker gained access and extracted cloud credentials, an LLM agent autonomously executed a chain of attacks to retrieve an SSH key and access an internal database, completing the full exploitation in less than one hour. The deployment failure was the absence of access controls or runtime monitoring that would have detected and blocked the agent's unauthorized lateral movement and database queries.

The agent demonstrated reasoning across attack steps rather than executing a fixed script, using commands tailored to the discovered system architecture and reformatting output for machine consumption. This required no human operator to manually execute each stage, which is not established to have occurred. Whether this represents a genuine shift in attacker methods or remains an isolated incident is not established.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team discovered an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent executed a sophisticated attack in real time rather than following a pre-written script. An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access, then extracted cloud credentials from the compromised system. The attacker used these credentials to retrieve an SSH key from Amazon Web Services and accessed an internal database server. The entire attack, from initial compromise to stealing a complete database, took less than one hour. Throughout the process, the attacker used Cloudflare Workers to mask their location by spreading 12 API calls across eleven different IP addresses within 22 seconds.

The key finding was that an AI agent directed the attack rather than a human or automated script. Evidence included improvised database commands targeting tables that should not have existed, planning comments in Chinese mixed with English commands, output formatted specifically for machine consumption rather than human review, and the attack chain pulling data from previous commands to inform subsequent actions. The researchers emphasized that this represents a shift in attack economics, where attackers now use general artificial intelligence knowledge instead of building specific target-focused playbooks. They recommend immediately updating marimo software, rotating all credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection throughout networks.
